exemplary: a. 可仿效的；可做模范的
impoverish: t. 使贫穷；耗尽...的力气

articles.title: 完型 · G.I. Joe与普通美国士兵
articles.context: G.I. Joe的历史含义与二战普通士兵形象。带一点历史叙事感，但不煽情。
rows: Millions of Americans and foreigners see G.I. Joe as a mindless war toy, the symbol of American military adventurism, but that’s not how it used to be.
数百万美国人和外国人把G.I. Joe看成一种没有思想的战争玩具，甚至视为美国军事冒险主义的象征，但它过去并不是这样的。
explain

To the men and women who served in World War Ⅱ and the people they liberated, the G.I. was the common man grown into hero, the poor farm kid torn away from his home, the guy who bore all the burdens of battle, who slept in cold foxholes, who went without the necessities of food and shelter, who stuck it out and drove back the Nazi reign of murder.
对于那些参加过二战的男女，以及被他们解放的人来说，G.I.代表的是由普通人成长为英雄的形象：一个被迫离开家乡的贫穷农家孩子，一个承担全部战斗重负的人；他睡在寒冷的散兵坑里，缺少食物和住所等基本生活必需品，却仍坚持到底，最终击退纳粹的杀戮统治。
explain
This was not a volunteer soldier, not someone well paid, but an average guy, up against the best trained, best equipped, fiercest, most brutal enemies seen in centuries.
这不是一名志愿兵，也不是一个收入优厚的职业军人，而只是一个普通人，却要面对数百年来训练最严格、装备最好、最凶悍、最残酷的一批敌人。
explain
His name isn’t much. G.I. is just a military abbreviation meaning Government Issue, and it was on all of the articles handed out to soldiers.
这个名字本身并不起眼。G.I.只是“Government Issue（政府配发）”的军事缩写，这几个字曾印在所有发给士兵的物品上。
explain
And Joe?
至于Joe，
explain
A common name for a guy who never made it to the top.
不过是一个普通人的名字，一个从来没有飞黄腾达的家伙：
explain
Joe Blow, Joe Palooka, Joe Magrac...a working class name.
Joe Blow、Joe Palooka、Joe Magrac……都是工人阶层色彩浓厚的名字。
explain
The United States has never had a president or vice-president or secretary of state Joe. G.I. Joe had a distinguished career fighting German, Japanese, and Korean troops.
美国历史上从未有叫Joe的总统、副总统或国务卿。G.I. Joe有过一段显赫的军旅生涯，与德国、日本和朝鲜军队作战。
explain
He appears as a character, or a collection of American personalities, in the 1945 movie The Story of G.I. Joe, based on the last days of war correspondent Ernie Pyle.
他以一个角色——或者说一组美国人格的集合——出现在1945年的电影《G.I. Joe的故事》中，该片取材自战地记者厄尼·派尔生命最后阶段的经历。
explain
Some of the soldiers Pyle interviewed portrayed themselves in the film.
派尔采访过的一些士兵还在电影中扮演了自己。
explain
Pyle was famous for covering the human side of the war, writing about the dirt-snow-and-mud soldiers, not how many miles were gained or what towns were captured or liberated.
派尔以报道战争中“人的一面”而著名；他写的是满身泥雪尘土的士兵，而不是推进了多少英里，或攻占、解放了哪些城镇。
explain
His reports paralleled the “Willie” cartoons of famed Stars and Stripes artist Bill Maulden.
他的报道与《星条旗报》著名画家比尔·莫尔丁笔下的“威利”漫画相互呼应。
explain
Both men emphasized the dirt and exhaustion of war, the fragments of civilization that the soldiers shared with each other and the civilians: coffee, tobacco, whiskey, shelter, sleep.
两个人都着重表现战争的污浊与疲惫，以及士兵彼此、以及士兵与平民共同珍视的文明碎片：咖啡、烟草、威士忌、住所和睡眠。
explain
To Egypt, France, and a dozen more countries, G.I. Joe was any American soldier, at that point the most important person in their lives.
对于埃及、法国以及另外十几个国家的人来说，G.I. Joe就是任何一名美国士兵——在当时，那些士兵是他们生活中最重要的人。
explain

articles.title: 阅读一 · 家庭作业该占多少分
articles.context: 洛杉矶学区家庭作业政策争议。语气分析、克制，突出政策目标与副作用。
rows: Homework has never been terribly popular with students and even many parents, but in recent years it has been particularly scorned.
家庭作业从来没有特别受学生欢迎，甚至很多家长也不喜欢；近些年，它更是受到明显轻视。
explain
School districts across the country, most recently Los Angeles Unified, are revising their thinking on this educational ritual.
美国各地学区都在重新思考这一教育惯例，最近的例子是洛杉矶联合学区。
explain

Unfortunately, L.A. Unified has produced an inflexible policy which mandates that with the exception of some advanced courses, homework may no longer count for more than 10% of a student’s academic grade.
遗憾的是，该学区制定了一项过于僵硬的政策：除少数高级课程外，家庭作业在学生学业成绩中的占比不得超过10%。
explain
This rule is meant to address the difficulty that students from impoverished or chaotic homes might have in completing their homework.
这项规定原本是为了解决这样一个困难——来自贫困或家庭生活混乱环境的学生，可能难以完成作业。
explain
But the policy is unclear and contradictory.
然而，这项政策本身含糊而矛盾。
explain
Certainly, no homework should be assigned that students cannot complete on their own or that they cannot do without expensive equipment.
当然，不应布置学生无法独立完成、或必须借助昂贵设备才能完成的作业。
explain

But if the district is essentially giving a pass to students who do not do their homework because of complicated family lives, it is going riskily close to the implication that standards need to be lowered for poor children.
但如果学区因为一些学生家庭情况复杂、没有完成作业，就事实上对他们“放行”，那就危险地接近这样一种暗示：对贫困儿童，标准就应该降低。
explain
District administrators say that homework will still be a part of schooling; teachers are allowed to assign as much of it as they want.
学区管理者说，家庭作业仍然是学校教育的一部分，教师想布置多少都可以。
explain
But with homework counting for no more than 10% of their grades, students can easily skip half their homework and see very little difference on their report cards.
但既然作业最多只占成绩的10%，学生即使跳过一半作业，成绩单上也几乎看不出差别。
explain
Some students might do well on state tests without completing their homework, but what about the students who performed well on the tests and did their homework?
有些学生不做作业也能在州统一考试中取得好成绩，但那些既考试成绩好、又认真完成作业的学生呢？
explain
It is quite possible that the homework helped.
完全可能正是作业帮助了他们。
explain
Yet rather than empowering teachers to find what works best for their students, the policy imposes a flat, across-the-board rule.
然而，这项政策不是赋予教师权力，让他们针对自己的学生寻找最有效的方法，而是强行施加一条一刀切的规定。
explain
At the same time, the policy addresses none of the truly thorny questions about homework.
与此同时，它没有触及家庭作业真正棘手的问题。
explain
If the district finds homework to be unimportant to its students’ academic achievement, it should move to reduce or eliminate the assignments, not make them count for almost nothing.
如果学区认为作业对学生的学业成就并不重要，就应该减少甚至取消作业，而不是让它几乎不计分；
explain
Conversely, if homework matters, it should account for a significant portion of the grade.
反过来，如果作业确实重要，就应该在成绩中占有显著比例。
explain

Meanwhile, this policy does nothing to ensure that the homework students receive is meaningful or appropriate to their age and the subject, or that teachers are not assigning more than they are willing to review and correct.
此外，这项政策也无法确保学生收到的作业真正有意义、适合其年龄和学科，也无法保证教师不会布置超过自己愿意批改和反馈能力的作业。
explain
The homework rules should be put on hold while the school board, which is responsible for setting educational policy, looks into the matter and conducts public hearings.
学校董事会负责制定教育政策，在其调查此事并举行公开听证会期间，应暂停执行这些作业规定。
explain
It is not too late for L.A. Unified to do homework right.
洛杉矶联合学区现在重新把“家庭作业”这件事做对，还不算太晚。
explain

articles.title: 阅读二 · 粉色如何被塑造成“女孩色”
articles.context: 粉色、性别编码与儿童营销。语气带反思感，强调所谓“自然偏好”背后的商业塑造。
rows: Pretty in pink: adult women do not remember being so obsessed with the colour, yet it is pervasive in our young girls’ lives.
“粉红真漂亮”：成年的女性并不记得自己小时候曾如此迷恋这种颜色，可如今粉红色却几乎充斥着小女孩的生活。
explain

It is not that pink is intrinsically bad, but it is such a tiny slice of the rainbow and, though it may celebrate girlhood in one way, it also repeatedly and firmly fuses girls’ identity to appearance.
问题并不是粉红色本身有什么不好，而是它只是彩虹中极小的一部分；它也许以某种方式赞美了女孩时代，却又不断而坚定地把女孩的身份与外表绑在一起。
explain
Then it presents that connection, even among two-year-olds, between girls as not only innocent but as evidence of innocence.
更进一步，这种关联甚至从两岁左右就被呈现为不仅天真无害，而且仿佛还是“天真”的证据。
explain
Looking around, I despaired at the singular lack of imagination about girls’ lives and interests.
环顾四周，我对人们想象女孩生活和兴趣时如此单一贫乏感到失望。
explain
Girls’ attraction to pink may seem unavoidable, somehow encoded in their DNA, but according to Jo Paoletti, an associate professor of American Studies, it is not.
女孩对粉红色的偏爱似乎不可避免，仿佛写进了DNA，但美国研究副教授乔·保莱蒂认为事实并非如此。
explain

Children were not colour-coded at all until the early 20th century: in the era before domestic washing machines all babies wore white as a practical matter, since the only way of getting clothes clean was to boil them.
直到20世纪初，儿童根本没有按颜色区分性别。在没有家用洗衣机的年代，为了实用，所有婴儿都穿白色衣服，因为只有煮洗才能把衣服洗干净。
explain
What’s more, both boys and girls wore what were thought of as gender-neutral dresses.
更何况，当时男孩和女孩穿的都是被视为性别中性的裙装。
explain
When nursery colours were introduced, pink was actually considered the more masculine colour, a pastel version of red, which was associated with strength.
托儿室颜色出现后，粉红色反而被看作更男性化的颜色——它是红色的浅色版本，而红色与力量相联系。
explain
Blue, with its intimations of the Virgin Mary, constancy and faithfulness, symbolised femininity.
蓝色由于让人联想到圣母玛利亚、忠贞与信仰，反而象征女性气质。
explain

It was not until the mid-1980s, when amplifying age and sex differences became a dominant children’s marketing strategy, that pink fully came into its own, when it began to seem inherently attractive to girls, part of what defined them as female, at least for the first few critical years.
直到20世纪80年代中期，放大年龄和性别差异成为儿童营销的主导策略，粉红色才真正“属于”女孩：它开始显得天生就对女孩有吸引力，仿佛成为界定女性身份的一部分，至少在人生最初几个关键年份如此。
explain
I had not realised how profoundly marketing trends dictated our perception of what is natural to kids, including our core beliefs about their psychological development.
我此前从未意识到，营销趋势竟如此深刻地支配着我们对“儿童天性”的认识，甚至影响我们对儿童心理发展的核心信念。
explain
Take the toddler.
以“幼儿”这个概念为例。
explain
I assumed that phase was something experts developed after years of research into children’s behaviour: wrong.
我原以为这个阶段是专家经过多年儿童行为研究后划分出来的；事实并非如此。
explain
Turns out, according to Daniel Cook, a historian of childhood consumerism, it was popularised as a marketing trick by clothing manufacturers in the 1930s.
儿童消费史学者丹尼尔·库克指出，“toddler（幼儿）”其实是20世纪30年代服装制造商作为营销技巧推广开的。
explain
Trade publications counselled department stores that, in order to increase sales, they should create a “third stepping stone” between infant wear and older kids’ clothes.
行业刊物建议百货商店，为了增加销售额，应在婴儿服装和大孩子服装之间人为创造“第三块踏脚石”。
explain
It was only after “toddler” became a common shoppers’ term that it evolved into a broadly accepted developmental stage.
直到“toddler”成为购物者的常用词，它才逐渐演变为一个广泛接受的发展阶段。
explain
Splitting kids, or adults, into ever-tinier categories has proved a sure-fire way to boost profits.
把儿童或成年人切分成越来越细小的类别，已经被证明是一种可靠的增利手段。
explain
And one of the easiest ways to segment a market is to magnify gender differences – or invent them where they did not previously exist.
而细分市场最容易的方法之一，就是放大性别差异——或者在原本不存在差异的地方发明差异。
explain

articles.title: 阅读三 · 基因专利之争
articles.context: DNA与基因专利法律争议。语气理性，法院判决、产业立场与反对理由层次分明。
rows: In 2010, a federal judge shook America’s biotech industry to its core.
2010年，一名联邦法官的判决震动了美国生物技术产业。
explain
Companies had won patents for isolated DNA for decades – by 2005 some 20% of human genes were patented.
几十年来，企业一直能够为分离出来的DNA取得专利；到2005年，大约20%的人类基因已经被申请专利。
explain
But in March 2010 a judge ruled that genes were unpatentable.
但2010年3月，一名法官裁定基因本身不可申请专利，
explain
Executives were violently agitated.
企业高管顿时高度紧张。
explain
The Biotechnology Industry Organisation (BIO), a trade group, assured members that this was just a “preliminary step” in a longer battle.
行业组织美国生物技术产业组织安抚会员说，这只是漫长法律斗争中的“初步一步”。
explain
On July 29th they were relieved, at least temporarily.
7月29日，他们至少暂时松了一口气：
explain
A federal appeals court overturned the prior decision, ruling that Myriad Genetics could indeed hold patents to two genes that help forecast a woman’s risk of breast cancer.
一家联邦上诉法院推翻此前裁决，认定Myriad Genetics确实可以持有两个基因的专利，而这两个基因可帮助预测女性乳腺癌风险。
explain
The chief executive of Myriad, a company in Utah, said the ruling was a blessing to firms and patients alike.
位于犹他州的Myriad公司首席执行官称，这项判决对企业和患者双方都是福音。
explain
But as companies continue their attempts at personalised medicine, the courts will remain rather busy.
但随着企业继续推进个体化医疗，法院恐怕仍会十分忙碌，
explain
The Myriad case itself is probably not over.
Myriad案本身也很可能尚未结束。
explain

Critics make three main arguments against gene patents: a gene is a product of nature, so it may not be patented; gene patents suppress innovation rather than reward it; and patents’ monopolies restrict access to genetic tests such as Myriad’s.
反对基因专利的人主要提出三点理由：第一，基因是自然产物，因此不应获得专利；第二，基因专利并非奖励创新，反而会压制创新；第三，专利形成的垄断会限制人们获得基因检测的机会，例如Myriad提供的检测。
explain
A growing number seem to agree.
越来越多人似乎赞同这些观点。
explain
Last year a federal task-force urged reform for patents related to genetic tests.
去年，一个联邦工作组敦促改革与基因检测相关的专利制度。
explain

In October the Department of Justice filed a brief in the Myriad case, arguing that an isolated DNA molecule “is no less a product of nature…than are cotton fibres that have been separated from cotton seeds.”
10月，美国司法部在Myriad案中提交意见书，指出一段被分离出来的DNA分子“并不比从棉籽中分离出来的棉纤维更不像自然产物”。
explain
Despite the appeals court’s decision, big questions remain unanswered.
尽管上诉法院已经作出判决，很多重大问题仍没有答案。
explain
For example, it is unclear whether the sequencing of a whole genome violates the patents of individual genes within it.
例如，对完整基因组进行测序，是否会侵犯其中单个基因的专利，目前仍不清楚。
explain
The case may yet reach the Supreme Court.
这个案子最终仍可能进入最高法院。
explain
As the industry advances, however, other suits may have an even greater impact.
不过，随着产业发展，其他诉讼也许会产生更大影响。
explain
Companies are unlikely to file many more patents for human DNA molecules – most are already patented or in the public domain.
企业不太可能再大量申请人类DNA分子的专利——大多数早已被专利覆盖，或者已经进入公有领域。
explain
Firms are now studying how genes interact, looking for correlations that might be used to determine the causes of disease or predict a drug’s efficacy.
如今，企业开始研究基因如何相互作用，寻找能够用于判定疾病原因或预测药物疗效的相关关系。
explain
Companies are eager to win patents for “connecting the dots,” explains Hans Sauer, a lawyer for the BIO.
BIO律师汉斯·绍尔解释说，企业非常希望为这种“把点连起来”的发现赢得专利。
explain
Their success may be determined by a suit related to this issue, brought by the Mayo Clinic, which the Supreme Court will hear in its next term.
而它们能否成功，可能取决于与这一问题有关的一桩诉讼；该案由梅奥诊所提起，最高法院将在下一个审期审理。
explain
The BIO recently held a convention which included sessions to coach lawyers on the shifting landscape for patents.
BIO最近召开的一次大会还专门设置了课程，指导律师应对不断变化的专利法律环境，
explain
Each meeting was packed.
而且场场爆满。
explain

articles.title: 阅读四 · 高失业时代如何改变社会
articles.context: 长期高失业对青年、阶层与社会性格的影响。语气沉稳，结尾保留不确定性与警示感。
rows: The great recession may be over, but this era of high joblessness is probably beginning.
大衰退也许已经结束，但高失业率的时代很可能才刚刚开始。
explain
Before it ends, it will likely change the life course and character of a generation of young adults.
在它结束之前，很可能会改变一代年轻人的人生轨迹和性格；
explain
And ultimately, it is likely to reshape our politics, our culture, and the character of our society for years.
最终，它还可能在多年里重塑我们的政治、文化以及整个社会的性格。
explain
No one tries harder than the jobless to find silver linings in this national economic disaster.
没有人比失业者更努力地从这场全国性的经济灾难中寻找一点“乌云背后的亮边”。
explain
Many said that unemployment, while extremely painful, had improved them in some ways: they had become less materialistic and more financially prudent; they were more aware of the struggles of others.
许多人说，失业虽然极其痛苦，却也在某些方面让自己变得更好：他们不再那么物质主义，理财更加谨慎，也更能意识到他人的艰难。
explain
In limited respects, perhaps the recession will leave society better off.
从有限角度看，这场衰退也许会让社会在某些方面有所改善。
explain
At the very least, it has awoken us from our national fever dream of easy riches and bigger houses, and put a necessary end to an era of reckless personal spending.
至少，它让我们从“轻松致富、房子越大越好”的全国性狂热梦中惊醒，并给一个个人肆意消费的时代画上了必要的句号。
explain
But for the most part, these benefits seem thin, uncertain, and far off.
但总体而言，这些好处看上去很微薄、不确定，而且遥远。
explain

In The Moral Consequences of Economic Growth, the economic historian Benjamin Friedman argues that both inside and outside the U.S., lengthy periods of economic stagnation or decline have almost always left society more mean-spirited and less inclusive, and have usually stopped or reversed the advance of rights and freedoms.
经济史学家本杰明·弗里德曼在《经济增长的道德后果》中指出，无论在美国国内还是国外，长期的经济停滞或衰退几乎总会使社会变得更刻薄、更排外，也往往会阻止甚至逆转权利与自由的发展。
explain
Anti-immigrant sentiment typically increases, as does conflict between races and classes.
反移民情绪通常会上升，种族和阶层之间的冲突也会加剧。
explain
Income inequality usually falls during a recession, but it has not shrunk in this one.
经济衰退期间，收入不平等通常会下降，但这一次并没有缩小。
explain
Indeed, this period of economic weakness may reinforce class divides, and decrease opportunities to cross them – especially for young people.
事实上，这段经济疲弱时期可能进一步强化阶层分化，并减少跨越阶层的机会，尤其对年轻人如此。
explain

The research of Till Von Wachter, the economist at Columbia University, suggests that not all people graduating into a recession see their life chances dimmed: those with degrees from elite universities catch up fairly quickly to where they otherwise would have been if they had graduated in better times; it is the masses beneath them that are left behind.
哥伦比亚大学经济学家蒂尔·冯·瓦赫特的研究表明，并不是所有在经济衰退期毕业的人都会长期失去机会。名校毕业生能够比较快地追上他们在景气时期毕业本应达到的位置；真正被甩在后面的，是他们之下的大多数人。
explain
In the Internet age, it is particularly easy to see the resentment that has always been hidden within American society.
互联网时代尤其容易让人看见美国社会内部一直存在、过去较为隐蔽的怨恨。
explain
More difficult, in the moment, is discerning precisely how these lean times are affecting society’s character.
更困难的是，在当下准确判断这些艰难岁月究竟如何改变社会性格。
explain
In many respects, the U.S. was more socially tolerant entering this recession than at any time in its history, and a variety of national polls on social conflict since then have shown mixed results.
在很多方面，美国进入这次衰退时，比历史上任何时期都更加社会宽容；此后围绕社会冲突的多项全国民调也呈现混合结果。
explain
We will have to wait and see exactly how these hard times will reshape our social fabric.
我们还需要等待，才能看清这些困难时期究竟会怎样重塑社会肌理。
explain
But they certainly will reshape it, and all the more so the longer they extend.
但可以肯定，它们一定会重塑社会，而且持续得越久，影响越深。
explain

articles.title: 新题型 · 从伟人史到大众史
articles.context: 西方史学从伟人传记转向阶级、大众与社会史。人物引语较多，保持思想史脉络感。
rows: “Universal history, the history of what man has accomplished in this world, is at bottom the History of the Great Men who have worked here,” wrote the Victorian sage Thomas Carlyle.
维多利亚时代思想家托马斯·卡莱尔写道：“普遍历史，也就是人类在这个世界上完成了什么的历史，从根本上说，就是那些在这里活动过的伟人的历史。”
explain
Well, not any more it is not.
如今，情况已经不再如此。
explain
Suddenly, Britain looks to have fallen out with its favorite historical form.
英国似乎突然与自己最喜爱的历史叙事形式产生了隔阂。
explain

This could be no more than a passing literary craze, but it also points to a broader truth about how we now approach the past: less concerned with learning from our forefathers and more interested in feeling their pain.
这可能只是一阵短暂的文学风潮，却也揭示了我们今天面对过去时的一项更广泛事实：我们越来越少想着向祖辈学习，而越来越关心去感受他们的痛苦。
explain
Today, we want empathy, not inspiration.
今天，我们需要的是共情，而不是榜样式的激励。
explain
From the earliest days of the Renaissance, the writing of history meant recounting the exemplary lives of great men.
从文艺复兴最早期开始，写历史就意味着讲述伟人的典范人生。
explain
In 1337, Petrarch began work on his rambling writing De Viris Illustribus – On Famous Men, highlighting the virtus (or virtue) of classical heroes.
1337年，彼特拉克开始撰写篇幅庞杂的《名人传》，突出古典英雄的virtus，也就是德性。
explain
Petrarch celebrated their greatness in conquering fortune and rising to the top.
他赞颂这些人物战胜命运、登上顶峰的伟大。
explain
This was the biographical tradition which Niccolò Machiavelli turned on its head.
这种传记传统后来被尼科洛·马基雅维利彻底翻转。
explain
In The Prince, he championed cunning, ruthlessness, and boldness, rather than virtue, mercy and justice, as the skills of successful leaders.
在《君主论》中，他认为成功领袖所需要的技能是机敏、冷酷和大胆，而不是德性、仁慈与正义。
explain
Over time, the attributes of greatness shifted.
随着时间推移，人们对“伟大”的理解也在变化。
explain
The Romantics commemorated the leading painters and authors of their day, stressing the uniqueness of the artist’s personal experience rather than public glory.
浪漫主义者纪念当时最重要的画家和作家，强调艺术家个人经验的独特性，而不是公共荣耀。
explain
By contrast, the Victorian author Samuel Smiles wrote Self -Help as a catalogue of the worthy lives of engineers, industrialists and explorers.
与此相反，维多利亚时代作家塞缪尔·斯迈尔斯在《自助》中罗列工程师、工业家和探险家的可敬人生。
explain

“The valuable examples which they furnish of the power of self-help, of patient purpose, resolute working, and steadfast integrity, issuing in the formation of truly noble and manly character, exhibit,” wrote Smiles, “what it is in the power of each to accomplish for himself.”
他写道，这些人的人生展示了自助、耐心的目标、坚定劳动和不动摇的正直所具有的力量，并由此形成真正高尚而坚强的品格；这些范例说明，每个人都有能力靠自己取得成就。
explain
His biographies of James Watt, Richard Arkwright and Josiah Wedgwood were held up as beacons to guide the working man through his difficult life.
他为詹姆斯·瓦特、理查德·阿克赖特和乔赛亚·韦奇伍德所作的传记，被树立为灯塔，引导普通劳动者走过艰难生活。
explain
This was all a bit bourgeois for Thomas Carlyle, who focused his biographies on the truly heroic lives of Martin Luther, Oliver Cromwell and Napoleon Bonaparte.
对托马斯·卡莱尔而言，这一套多少显得太过资产阶级化，因此他把传记写作聚焦于马丁·路德、奥利弗·克伦威尔和拿破仑·波拿巴这些真正英雄式的人生。
explain
These epochal figures represented lives hard to imitate, but to be acknowledged as possessing higher authority than mere mortals.
这些划时代人物的人生难以模仿，却被认为拥有高于普通凡人的权威。
explain
Not everyone was convinced by such bombast.
并非所有人都相信这种夸张的伟人崇拜。
explain
“The history of all hitherto existing society is the history of class struggles,” wrote Marx and Engels in The Communist Manifesto.
马克思和恩格斯在《共产党宣言》中写道：“至今一切社会的历史都是阶级斗争的历史。”
explain
For them, history did nothing, it possessed no immense wealth nor waged battles: “It is man, real, living man who does all that.”
在他们看来，历史本身不会做任何事，也不拥有巨大财富，更不会亲自发动战争；真正完成这一切的是“人，现实的、活生生的人”。
explain
And history should be the story of the masses and their record of struggle, As such, it needed to appreciate the economic realities, the social contexts and power relations in which each epoch stood.
因此，历史应该讲述大众以及他们斗争的记录，也应该理解每个时代所处的经济现实、社会背景和权力关系。
explain

For: “Men make their own history, but they do not make it just as they please; they do not make it under circumstances chosen by themselves, but under circumstances directly found, given and transmitted from the past.”
正如那句著名的话：“人们自己创造自己的历史，但他们并不是随心所欲地创造，并不是在自己选定的条件下创造，而是在直接碰到的、既定的、从过去继承下来的条件下创造。”
explain
This was the tradition which revolutionised our appreciation of the past.
正是这一传统彻底改变了我们理解过去的方式。
explain
In place of Thomas Carlyle, Britain nurtured Christopher Hill, EP Thompson and Eric Hobsbawm.
英国不再只有卡莱尔，也孕育出克里斯托弗·希尔、E.P.汤普森和埃里克·霍布斯鲍姆。
explain
History from below stood alongside biographies of great men.
“自下而上的历史”与伟人传记并立。
explain
Whole new realms of understanding – from gender to race to cultural studies – were opened up as scholars unpicked the multiplicity of lost societies.
随着学者拆解那些已经消失社会的复杂多样性，从性别、种族到文化研究，一个又一个全新的理解领域被打开。
explain
And it transformed public history too: downstairs became just as fascinating as upstairs.
公共历史也随之改变：楼下普通人的生活，终于和楼上精英的生活一样值得研究。
explain

articles.title: 翻译 · “人才流失”之忧
articles.context: 发展中国家的人才外流及其经济担忧。语气客观，数字和因果关系清晰。
rows: When people in developing countries worry about migration, they are usually concerned at the prospect of their best and brightest departure to Silicon Valley or to hospitals and universities in the developed world.
当发展中国家的人谈到移民问题时，他们通常担心的是：本国最优秀、最聪明的人才会离开，前往硅谷，或去发达国家的医院和大学工作。
explain
These are the kind of workers that countries like Britain, Canada and Australia try to attract by using immigration rules that privilege college graduates.
英国、加拿大、澳大利亚等国家正是希望吸引这类劳动者，因此其移民规则往往优待大学毕业生。
explain
Lots of studies have found that well-educated people from developing countries are particularly likely to emigrate.
大量研究发现，发展中国家受教育程度较高的人尤其容易移居国外。
explain
A big survey of Indian households in 2004 found that nearly 40% of emigrants had more than a high-school education, compared with around 3.3% of all Indians over the age 25.
2004年对印度家庭进行的一项大型调查发现，移民者中近40%接受过高中以上教育，而25岁以上印度人口中这一比例只有约3.3%。
explain
This “brain drain” has long bothered policymakers in poor countries.
这种“人才流失”长期以来一直困扰着贫穷国家的政策制定者。
explain

They fear that it hurts their economies, depriving them of much-needed skilled workers who could have taught at their universities, worked in their hospitals and come up with clever new products for their factories to make.
他们担心，这会损害本国经济，因为这些国家会失去迫切需要的高技能劳动者——这些人本可以在大学任教、在医院工作，或者为本国工厂想出聪明的新产品。
explain
